title: Therac-25 radiation overdoses: software interlocks, misleading machine state, and medical-device attribution failure
summary: Therac-25 is promoted as a canonical but high-sensitivity software-safety case. Rev0011 encodes it around software-mediated radiation overdoses, missing or weakened independent safeguards, misleading operator feedback, and the danger of reducing complex accidents to “human error.”

type_payload.incident_class: medical-device software safety accidents / attribution and interlock failure

sequence_of_events.event: Therac-25 was deployed with more software responsibility and fewer hardware interlocks than predecessor designs.
A series of overdose accidents occurred across clinical sites.
Misleading machine feedback, inadequate independent detection, and software/race/data-entry failure paths complicated attribution and operator response.
The machine was recalled for design changes, including hardware safeguards against software errors.

type_payload.proximate_cause: Multiple software-mediated overdose paths with misleading operator feedback and insufficient independent safeguards/detection.
